title: Full second-order validity: why no effective calculus is complete

based_on.title: Undecidability, Incompleteness, and Completeness of Second-Order Logic in Coq

summary: Turn arithmetic truth into full second-order validity by one effective sentence construction, and rule out sound, complete enumeration of validities.
abstract: A finite list of second-order arithmetic axioms determines the natural-number structure up to isomorphism. Can an effective proof calculus capture every sentence true in every full second-order structure? If it could, we could recognize every true arithmetic sentence by looking for a proof of a suitable implication. We construct that implication, check its effect on actual sentence codes, and use the non-enumerability of true arithmetic to prove that full second-order validities cannot be enumerated. Every sound calculus whose theorem codes can be enumerated consequently misses a validity. This concerns completeness even for sentences with no premises, and explains a sharper boundary than failure of compactness alone.
